## Summary

Taught **O3** (context and memory in an agent) as a 30-minute lesson, grounded in two sources I read this session: Anthropic's ["Effective context engineering for AI agents"](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents) and IBM's ["What Is Context Engineering?"](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/context-engineering) — both logged in the new `RESOURCES.md`.

**Written:**
- `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html` — context window as a shared token budget, context rot within a session, sessions starting empty by default, and notes vs. retrieval as the two memory patterns, all tied to the makerspace assistant's manual search and training records. ~26 minutes of reading.
- `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html` — one-page reference for the terms and the notes-vs-retrieval table.
- `quizzes/0002.json` + `keys/0002.json` — 5 fresh items on O3, none repeating the lesson's practice checks.
- `NOTES.md` updated with what was taught and three new misconceptions (**M7**: bigger context = more reliable; **M8**: searchable = already read; **M9**: standing/input tokens don't really cost), plus a callback to **M3**.

Riley still has quiz 0001 (two ungraded attempts) and this new quiz 0002 sitting pending — happy to grade either whenever they're ready, or just answer questions about today's lesson in the chat.
